a: Give its meaning and differentiate between Stock and Supply? Answers: Supply Definition: Supply is defined as "The number of goods and services offered for sale at a given price in the market", e.g. 500 K.g. of sugar is provided in the market for sale; this quantity of sugar is called its "Supply", in Economics. Differentiate Between Stock and Supply: Stock is the total volume of a commodity that can be brought into the market for the purpose of sale at a short notice; while supply means the amount offered for sale at a given price. e.g. The present quantity of sugar in the market is 8000 K.g. and out of it only 5,000 K.3. of sugar is offered for sale. In this case, 8,000 K.g. of sugar is the stock, and 5,000 K.g. is called the supply of sugar. Supply is closely relevant to price as the volume of supply is determined by the fall and rise in price. That is why the larger quantities are offered for sale from the stock if the price is high. And if the price is low, only the smaller quantities are offered for sale. It is, because of the higher prices that the profit of suppliers increases. So, they increase the supply to earn more and more profit. Inversely, when prices fall; the profit also falls down. In this case, the suppliers supply less quantity for sale to minimize their loss.
